VINIT.justification: The state of the host Python process before activate_this.py is executed.

TANCH.justification: The terminal anchor that seals the environment boundary to the base directory.

AFWD.justification: Forward transformation adding new library paths to the import mechanism.

AREV.justification: Contravariant transformation reordering the path to prioritize the virtual environment.

CLINK.justification: Sequential chaining of path components to derive absolute locations.

IMSCRIB.justification: Identity reference preserving the original host state within the new state.

FSPLIT.justification: Splits a bipartite graph into two distinct node sets: top and bottom.

FFUSE.justification: Reconstitutes the bipartite structure by joining the two node sets with all possible edges.

EVALT.justification: Affirmative evaluation where the LibYAML-based parser is present.

EVALF.justification: Negative evaluation resulting in an exception when a module is missing.

ENGAGR.justification: A paradice holding both the presence and absence of edges simultaneously to save memory.

IFIX.justification: Permanent irreversible record of the environment variables for the process duration.

steps.domain_action: host interpreter starts in uninitialized state
os.path.abspath(__file__) derives the activation script path
os.path.dirname(abs_file) locates the bin directory
os.environ['VIRTUAL_ENV'] is fixed to the base directory
os.environ['VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT'] is fixed to Voynich_Phytoglyphica
site.addsitedir appends the phytoglyphica site-packages to the search space
sys.path reordering moves the new paths to the front of the list
sys.real_prefix records the identity of the host interpreter
sys.prefix is anchored to the virtual environment base
bipartite.sets(G) decomposes the network into top and bottom phytoglyphs
check if the top set contains valid botanical identifiers
check if the bottom set contains invalid astronomical labels
complete_bipartite_graph(U, V) recovers the full phytoglyphic network
AntiGraph maintains the complement state for dense network analysis
networkx.algorithms.approximation.clique_removal begins iterative reduction
ramsey.ramsey_R2 splits the graph into a potential clique and independent set
the clique branch finds a maximal complete subgraph
the independent set branch finds a maximal non-connected subgraph
the results are fused to determine the next iteration of the graph
the final approximate maximum independent set is recorded in memory
